blocks.text: CANBERRA — An alleged Islamic State member has been arrested by counter-terrorism agents over allegations that he instructed people on how to plan and conduct mass-casualty attacks from his base in Australia. The Melbourne man, whom the Australian Federal Police alleges was a propagandist for the Islamic extremist group, is accused of sending about 10,000 documents, messages, images, videos and audio files relating to executions and torture. The 65-year-old allegedly pledged allegiance to ISIS, which stands for Islamic State of Iraq and Syria, and acted on its behalf without traveling to territory controlled by the terrorist organization during the conflict in […]...
